learning_outcomes.text: understand the main data structures and fundamental algorithm design techniques
understand the principles of computational complexity analysis in terms of time and space requirements
understand the operation and characteristics of fundamental algorithms for searching, sorting, graph traversal, and other classical computational problems
understand the role of algorithms in solving computational problems and in selected Artificial Intelligence applications
design and implement algorithms using appropriate algorithmic design techniques
select the most suitable data structures according to the characteristics of the problem
analyze and compare the efficiency of different algorithmic solutions
apply algorithms and data structures to solve programming problems of moderate complexity
evaluate the correctness and efficiency of algorithms and data structures
compare alternative algorithmic solutions and identify the most appropriate one for a given problem
justify the design choices adopted in the development of algorithmic solutions
describe algorithms, data structures, and their properties using appropriate technical terminology
explain the design choices and complexity analysis of the developed solutions, both orally and in writing
independently deepen their knowledge of algorithms, data structures, and algorithm design techniques
apply the acquired methodologies to new computational problems
build upon the acquired competencies in advanced Computer Engineering courses, including Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Databases, and Distributed Systems

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Algorithms and Complexity Analysis: Definition and properties of an algorithm
Computational problems, problem instances, and input size
Computational models and the RAM model
Asymptotic notation: O, Ω, and Θ
Analysis of iterative and recursive algorithms
Recurrence relations and the main methods for solving them
Amortized analysis and amortized cost of operations
Abstract Data Types and Fundamental Data Structures: Abstract data types, interfaces, and implementations
Sorting and Selection: Properties of sorting algorithms: stability, in-place sorting, adaptivity, and computational complexity
Elementary sorting algorithms: Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, and Shell Sort
Selection problems and the Quickselect algorithm
Priority Queues and Heaps: The priority queue abstract data type
Implementation and applications of priority queues
Searching and Symbol Tables: The symbol table or dictionary abstract data type and its implementations
Binary search trees and their operations
Balanced search trees: AVL trees and Red-Black trees
Graphs and Their Representations: Basic definitions and terminology
Connected components and strongly connected components
assessment_rules: The final examination consists of a practical laboratory test and an oral examination. In the practical laboratory test, students will design and implement an original solution to a given problem. In the interview, students must demonstrate theoretical and methodological knowledge, relevance of answers, quality of content, appropriate use of technical terminology, clarity of expression, ability to establish connections, and ability to provide appropriate examples. Accommodations for students with SLD, disabilities, or other special educational needs will be discussed with the instructor.
